entries.title: CPU (Processor)
entries.content: The CPU executes program instructions. Cores = parallel processing units; threads = virtual cores (hyper-threading). Clock speed in GHz (billions of cycles/sec). Cache L1/L2/L3 gives fast access to hot data. x86 (Intel/AMD) dominates desktops; ARM dominates phones (efficiency-first design).

entries.title: RAM (Memory)
entries.content: RAM is fast, temporary working memory — cleared on power off. DDR4/DDR5 are current generations (faster bus speeds). More RAM = more programs/processes held simultaneously. RAM (volatile, fast) vs Storage (non-volatile: SSD/HDD — holds data permanently). Typical: 8–16 GB RAM for a dev PC.

entries.title: Storage: HDD vs SSD
entries.content: HDD: spinning magnetic platters, cheap per GB (~₹2/GB), ~100-160 MB/s. SATA SSD: flash chips, no moving parts, ~550 MB/s. NVMe SSD: PCIe interface, 3000–7000 MB/s. Upgrade HDD→SSD is the single biggest speed boost for an old laptop. NAND flash has finite write cycles (TBW rating).

entries.title: OSI Model (7 Layers)
entries.content: OSI 7 layers: 7-Application (HTTP, user apps), 6-Presentation (encoding, TLS), 5-Session, 4-Transport (TCP/UDP, ports), 3-Network (IP, routers), 2-Data Link (MAC, switches), 1-Physical (cables, radio). Mnemonic: 'All People Seem To Need Data Processing'. TCP/IP is the practical 4-layer model used on the real internet.

entries.title: HTTP & DNS Basics
entries.content: DNS translates domain names (google.com) to server IPs — the internet's phonebook. HTTP methods: GET (read), POST (create/submit), PUT (replace), DELETE. HTTPS = HTTP + TLS encryption (padlock). Status codes: 200 OK, 301 redirect, 404 not found, 500 server error. Ports: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, DNS 53.

entries.title: Git Basics
entries.content: Git is distributed version control. Core flow: edit → git add (stage) → git commit (snapshot) → git push (upload to remote like GitHub). Branch = parallel line of work; merge = combine branches. git log shows history, git checkout/git switch changes branches, git clone downloads a repo. .gitignore excludes files from tracking.

entries.title: Python Basics
entries.content: Python is a high-level, dynamically-typed language. Core types: list [1,2], dict {'k':v}, tuple (immutable), set (unique). venv creates isolated environments (python -m venv .venv); pip installs packages (pip install requests). Zen of Python: 'import this' — Readability counts. Runs everywhere; the #1 language for AI/automation.

entries.title: Linux Essential Commands
entries.content: Everyday Linux: ls (list), cd (change dir), pwd (where am I), cp/mv/rm (copy/move/delete), mkdir, cat/less (view files), grep (search text), find (find files), chmod (permissions: r=4,w=2,x=1 → 755 = rwxr-xr-x), sudo (admin powers), apt/pip (install). Everything is a file — even devices (/dev).
